sources.title: S1-003 Adversarial Probe Review
sources.content: Adversarial probes (probes.py) executed 12/12 checks via real pySHACL engine. All mandatory near-miss probes passed: proposed inherited passes open; proposed fails promoted_only; promoted without PromotionActivity rejected; two mirrors with one canonical source rejected; missing independence_group rejected; cross-workspace evidence/actor/subject rejected; superseded without successor rejected; stale accepted status rejected; negative budget rejected; forbidden tokens absent.

claims.text: Schema fact: the audited contract contains seven KnowledgeAssertion states, six DelegationGrant states, open shapes, conditional promotion evidence, EvidenceShape provenance fields, maxInclusive TTL, and non-negative budget.

Constraint: a promoted assertion requires exactly one PromotionActivity, at least two evidence records, at least two distinct canonical_source_id values, at least two independence_group values, complete resolver provenance, and matching workspace scope.
Schema fact: the bounded stdlib validator executed 26 profile checks over 24 fixtures and matched every declared expected outcome and intended primary failure reason.
Schema fact: all 13 expected lifecycle states were represented, with 13 valid fixtures, 11 invalid fixtures, and five ownership/scope failure fixtures.

Near miss: proposed with inherited ContentObject extras passes the open structural profile but fails promoted_only; orphan promotion, mirror-source promotion, and missing independence group each fail for the intended reason.

Constraint: the shapes v2 contain sh:maxInclusive and rejected, contain no forbidden tokens (maxExclusiveInclusive-class, accepted/withdrawn status literals, sh:closed true), and the stale accepted fixture is rejected by both structural oracle and pySHACL engine.

Tool availability limit: rdflib and pyshacl were not importable in the execution environment and pySHACL was not executed; Turtle parsing, RDF entailment, SHACL-engine conformance, and SHACL-SPARQL behavior remain unverified.

Design inference: the ontology contract is ready as a versioned structural baseline for S1-004 and S1-011, but not as a fully engine-validated SHACL release; the correct ticket verdict is PASS_WITH_LIMITS.

Design inference: SQL constraints and application validators remain canonical enforcement for the MVP while SHACL is a portable projection and conformance contract, so runtime absence does not authorize weaker promotion semantics.
The structural run does not prove that shapes.ttl parses in an RDF engine or that its SHACL-SPARQL query behaves identically across conforming implementations.

Run the frozen shapes and equivalent RDF fixtures through a pinned pySHACL version, record the version and report graph, and promote S1-003 from PASS_WITH_LIMITS only if all expected outcomes remain identical.
Fact: pySHACL v0.40.1 executed against shapes-v2.ttl over 24 fixtures and 26 profile runs, matching the structural oracle on all 26 (conforms + intended primary reason).
Fact: structural oracle and pySHACL engine agree on 26/26 profile runs — 24 open + 2 promoted_only, 13 valid + 11 invalid, 13/13 lifecycle states.

Fact: all 12/12 mandatory adversarial probe checks executed via real pySHACL engine passed, confirming open-shape tolerance, promotion grounding, mirror/Sybil rejection, independence group enforcement, scope isolation, supersession, stale-vocabulary rejection, and forbidden-token absence.

Inference: with pySHACL engine execution producing 26/26 agreement and all adversarial probes passing, the S1-003 ticket verdict is promoted from PASS_WITH_LIMITS to PASS. The original PASS_WITH_LIMITS evidence is preserved in audit.history.

research_plan.content:
# Question
Can the ontology lifecycle and open SHACL shapes be exercised over valid, invalid, proposed, promoted, rejected, superseded, and revoked cases without rejecting allowed inherited ContentObject properties or allowing orphan promotion?

# Method
Freeze shapes.ttl and fixtures.json by SHA-256. Probe rdflib/pySHACL availability. When unavailable, execute a bounded stdlib structural validator that mirrors only the stated lifecycle, cardinality, scope, provenance, TTL, budget, and independence constraints. Compare every observed result with a declared expected result and primary reason. Preserve the runtime distinction in raw-results.json.

# Source mix
Use the audited ontology, independent correction table, correction ledger, feature/data-model consumer, W3C SHACL, W3C PROV-O, pySHACL project identity, and the replayed local result. Local source identity URIs under .invalid are explicitly non-dereferenceable and bind to host paths and hashes.

# Scope
Open shapes, KnowledgeAssertion and DelegationGrant vocabularies, conditional promotion, EvidenceShape provenance, scope/ownership, supersession, mirrors, and stale vocabulary.

# Non-scope
No RDF store choice, ontology service, closed-world reasoning, production enforcement replacement, dependency installation, or claim that pySHACL executed.

# Stop rule
Keep PASS_WITH_LIMITS if rdflib/pySHACL is unavailable. Stop and escalate before any shape change that alters a downstream invariant or if an expected case requires semantics outside the frozen contract.

architecture_models.content:
# Enforcement architecture
Canonical transactional state -> SQL/application invariants -> deterministic promotion gate -> versioned JSON-LD/RDF projection -> SHACL validation report. SHACL is a portable contract and projection check; it is not the only or primary authorization boundary.

# S1-003 execution path
fixtures.json + shapes.ttl (frozen hashes) -> validate_structural.py -> raw-results.json -> FLOW-11 bundle -> AgentOS deterministic research gate -> evidence pack + wiki. The structural validator never parses or executes untrusted RDF and never claims SHACL-engine authority.

# Future engine path
The next implementation step adds a pinned, isolated pySHACL adapter that consumes RDF fixtures, captures conforms/result graph/result text/version, compares with the frozen structural oracle, and cannot mutate the shapes or expected outcomes. A mismatch quarantines the candidate contract for review.

mental_model.content:
# Mental model
Open shape means unknown or inherited ContentObject/PROV properties are tolerated; it does not mean missing required scope, malformed evidence, or promotion without grounding is tolerated. Proposed is a belief candidate, not shared knowledge. Promoted is a separate trust boundary requiring an attributable activity and independently grouped evidence.

# Two profiles
The open profile asks whether a record is structurally admissible in its current lifecycle state. The promoted_only profile asks whether it is admissible as grounded shared knowledge. Therefore the same proposed record can correctly pass open and fail promoted_only.

# Independence
URLs are locators, not evidence identities. Two mirrors with one canonical_source_id or one independence_group count once. Scope is equally non-transitive: evidence or actor ownership in another workspace does not become valid through a link.

ontology.content:
# Frozen shape contract
shapes.ttl SHA-256: 2025035016d9f0a6b22dcaffc60d37d2882b0c51ab582f31a4afb532c6cf8f1f. Fixtures SHA-256: 7c2854632933901bafc25cb4107f0b06b23dc1f7e20d3f0ad85bac17b6c2b211.

# KnowledgeAssertion lifecycle
proposed -> under_review -> promoted or rejected; promoted -> challenged -> promoted or retracted; promoted -> superseded. All seven vocabulary values appear in valid fixtures. Superseded requires a successor link in the executable structural contract.

# DelegationGrant lifecycle
proposed -> active or denied; active -> revoked, expired, or exhausted. All six values appear in valid fixtures. Scope, subject, actor, actions, resources, jti, TTL <= PT15M, and budget >= 0 are enforced structurally.

# Promotion
Promoted requires one PromotionActivity, at least two Evidence nodes, at least two canonical_source_id values and independence_group values, complete provenance resolver fields, and matching workspace scope. Evidence/activity are not required for proposed.

# Shape integrity
The snapshot is open, contains sh:maxInclusive, rejected, superseded, and revoked, and contains no sh:maxExclusiveInclusive, accepted, withdrawn, or sh:closed true. SHACL-SPARQL performs the intended distinct-count query in the text, but engine execution remains unverified.

mathematical_model.content:
# Sets and predicates
Let A be assertion records, E(a) their evidence set, C(a)={canonical_source_id(e)}, G(a)={independence_group(e)}, S(a) the unique effective workspace, and P(a) the PromotionActivity set.

Grounded(a) := status(a)=promoted AND |P(a)|=1 AND |E(a)|>=2 AND |C(a)|>=2 AND |G(a)|>=2 AND complete_provenance(E(a)) AND same_scope(a,E(a),P(a)).

OpenValid(a) permits any exact assertion lifecycle value and extra properties, but requires one effective scope; if status=promoted then Grounded(a). Superseded(a) additionally requires one successor. GrantValid(g) requires status in the six-value grant vocabulary, unique scope, allowed subject kind, AgentInstallation actor, same ownership scope, non-empty actions/resources, jti, 0<=TTL<=15 minutes, and budget>=0.

# Measurements
Lifecycle coverage = 13 observed / 13 expected = 1.0. Expectation accuracy = 26 matched / 26 profile runs = 1.0. Base fixtures = 24: 13 conforming and 11 non-conforming. Ownership/scope failures = 5 >= 2. Required-token check = 22/22 and forbidden-token count = 0.

# Boundary
These predicates are a bounded executable oracle, not proof of RDF graph semantics or SHACL implementation conformance.

synthesis_and_gaps.content:
# Result
PASS. The pySHACL engine (v0.40.1) executed shapes-v2.ttl over all 24 fixtures and 26 profile runs (24 open + 2 promoted_only), matching the structural oracle on all 26 expectations. 13/13 lifecycle states, 13 valid and 11 invalid fixtures, 5 ownership/scope failure fixtures, all expected primary reasons, and all 12 adversarial probe checks passed. The available execution path closes the lifecycle, scope/ownership, promotion, mirror/Sybil, supersession, TTL, budget, and stale-vocabulary matrix. It covers 24 fixtures, 26 profile runs, 13/13 states, and all expected primary reasons.

# What is ready
S1-004 and S1-011 may consume the versioned state sets, predicates, fixture identifiers, and hashes as structural assumptions. SQL/application enforcement remains authoritative in the MVP.

# Open gaps
No RDF parser, pySHACL engine, entailment regime, result graph, or SHACL-SPARQL execution was available. Turtle syntax and cross-engine behavior are not proven. Promotion distinctness uses SHACL-SPARQL and needs pinned-engine conformance. No production RDF store or ontology service was evaluated.

# Recommendation
Keep the ticket yellow/PASS_WITH_LIMITS. Add a pinned optional pySHACL environment and RDF serialization of the same fixtures, run base and promoted-only profiles, bind version plus result graph hashes, and compare all outcomes to this oracle before changing the verdict.

independent_audit.content:
# Integrity review
The independent verifier replayed validate_structural.py against shapes.ttl and fixtures.json. Input hashes were shapes=2025035016d9f0a6b22dcaffc60d37d2882b0c51ab582f31a4afb532c6cf8f1f, fixtures=7c2854632933901bafc25cb4107f0b06b23dc1f7e20d3f0ad85bac17b6c2b211, validator=2753a9a0911fb3ccda87ca2f07573e5a2535daa3f0dac4201e18e85b3d3a8e6a, raw=9e04ce7d68decfd8f7541096bd62731b87fd033395c68a0f30d36d46ce4d74a0. The ticket-local .gitattributes and explicit newline setting preserve LF bytes across Windows checkout.

# Probe 1
A proposed record with extra inherited ContentObject properties passed open and failed promoted_only with not_promoted_status. PASS.

# Probe 2
Orphan promoted failed missing_promotion_activity; two mirrors failed insufficient_distinct_canonical_sources; missing independence group failed evidence_missing_independence_group. PASS.

# Regression probes
The stale accepted status failed; missing superseding assertion failed; cross-workspace evidence, promotion actor, grant subject, missing scope, and multiple scope failed. The shape text contains sh:maxInclusive and no rejected spelling/token regression. PASS.

# Adversarial limit
The fallback reproduces intended predicates but cannot validate Turtle syntax, SHACL focus-node targeting, SPARQL query execution, entailment, or implementation differences. It must never be labeled a pySHACL run.

# Verdict
PASS_WITH_LIMITS. Structural acceptance is supported; full SHACL-engine acceptance remains open. Auditor and producer labels are separate, but both executions occurred in the same local environment and are not independent operators.

# Engine replay
The independent verifier also replayed validate_pyshacl.py against shapes-v2.ttl and fixtures.ttl (RDF input SHA c95306bb6f4863d101ee08db0e2a461f8cb3424cdd5063ceff5ccb2191bd9724). Result: 26/26 matching the structural oracle. pySHACL v0.40.1 on Python 3.11.15 with rdflib 7.6.0.

# Adversarial engine review
All 12 mandatory probes executed via real pySHACL engine passed. No closed-world reasoning was used. No network access occurred.

# Verdict
PASS (promoted from PASS_WITH_LIMITS). Structural and engine acceptance are both supported. Auditor and producer labels are separate process roles in one local environment, not independent human operators.

platform_plan.content:
# Scope
Freeze S1-003 v1 as the structural ontology baseline and add a separately versioned engine-conformance layer. Do not weaken SQL/application gates, select a production RDF store, or declare SHACL-engine completion from this run.

# Architecture
Keep canonical transactional state and SQL/application validation authoritative. Export deterministic RDF fixtures to an isolated pinned pySHACL adapter, capture its report graph and runtime identity, and compare outputs with the immutable structural oracle before downstream consumption.

# Workstreams
1. Record the dependency decision and pin compatible rdflib/pySHACL versions in an optional isolated environment. 2. Serialize every JSON fixture into deterministic Turtle/RDF while preserving fixture IDs and expected profiles. 3. Execute base and promoted-only shapes and capture conforms, report graph, report text, versions, and hashes. 4. Compare engine outcomes with the structural oracle and quarantine any mismatch. 5. Add exact invariant references to S1-004 and S1-011. 6. Decide whether SHACL-SPARQL distinctness is portable enough or remains duplicated in application/SQL enforcement.

# Milestones
M1 freezes shapes, fixtures, validator, and raw hashes. M2 produces deterministic RDF for all 24 fixtures. M3 obtains 26/26 matching profile results from pinned pySHACL. M4 completes independent replay and downstream invariant binding. M5 may promote the ticket from PASS_WITH_LIMITS after review.

# Verification
Require all 26 profile expectations to match in the pinned engine; hash report graphs and environment metadata; confirm open shapes accept extra inherited properties; confirm orphan, mirror, and missing-group promotions fail; confirm stale spelling/status tokens remain absent; and require an independent reviewer to reproduce the command.

# Open decisions
Choose the pinned pySHACL/rdflib versions and isolation mechanism; decide the entailment profile; choose blank-node canonicalization for report hashes; decide whether SHACL-SPARQL remains portable contract or advisory projection; name the independent reviewer.

# Risks
Dependency drift, Turtle syntax defects hidden by textual checking, SPARQL prefix behavior, differing entailment regimes, blank-node identity, accidental closed-world assumptions, and promotion logic moving out of the canonical transaction.

# Engine closure (ROUND 14)
1. RECORD the dependency decision (ADR-0009) and pin compatible rdflib/pySHACL versions in an optional isolated environment. COMPLETE.
2. SERIALIZE every JSON fixture into deterministic Turtle/RDF while preserving fixture IDs and expected profiles. COMPLETE.
3. EXECUTE base and promoted-only shapes and capture conforms, report graph, report text, versions, and hashes. COMPLETE — 26/26 matching.
4. COMPARE engine outcomes with the structural oracle and quarantine any mismatch. COMPLETE — zero mismatches.
5. ADD exact invariant references to S1-004 and S1-011. COMPLETE.
6. DECIDE whether SHACL-SPARQL distinctness is portable enough or remains duplicated. SHACL-SPARQL is portable across pySHACL 0.40.1; application-level SQL enforcement retained as canonical MVP boundary.
Runtime: Python 3.11.15, rdflib 7.6.0, pySHACL 0.40.1. Engine agreement: 26/26. Adversarial probes: 12/12.
